chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Katib reported to me, who said: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi narrated to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to me, who said: al-Qasim ibn Yahya narrated to me, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Be it known to you that Allah, the Exalted, hates the fickle one among His creation. So do not slip away from the truth and its partisans, for indeed whoever seizes power through falsehood and its partisans shall perish, and shall lose this world and shall leave it humbled."

key_terms.استبد: Istabadda - To seize absolute power, to rule tyrannically, to act despotically
key_terms.الباطل: al-Batil - Falsehood, that which is vain and without substance
key_terms.الحق: al-Haqq - The truth, what is right and just
key_terms.المتلون: al-Mutalawwin - The fickle one, a person who constantly changes color/position, unreliable in their commitments
key_terms.صاغرا: Saghiran - Humbled, debased, in a state of degradation

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about fickleness and holding to the truth?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) admonishes the believers to remain steadfast in their commitment to truth. The term 'al-mutalawwin' (the fickle one) refers to someone who constantly shifts allegiances and convictions according to personal advantage. This teaching, delivered to the Imam's close companions, warns that those who rule through falsehood will ultimately face ruin in both this world and the next.
